findings.title: Call to undefined zero-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled breaks compilation
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but UsernamePasswordForm only defines isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user). AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator defines no such method. The code as shown does not compile, so the browser flow with UsernameForm cannot build/deploy.

findings.title: Conditional passkeys only filled when user is set breaks usernameless login
findings.body: authenticate() now calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm only if isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which requires user != null. For a fresh login context.getUser() is null, so no WebAuthn challenge / ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI is set on the initial username/password page. Discoverable passkeys / conditional UI therefore disappear on first login, contradicting the tests that expect form#webauth on the initial page.

findings.title: Error challenge also suppresses passkeys for anonymous users
findings.body: challenge(context,error,field) now only refills WebAuthn data when context.getUser() != null. Failed logins before a user is established (invalid username/password on the initial page) will re-render without the passkeys challenge, losing conditional UI after the first error.

findings.title: shouldShow overridden without shouldDisplay causes inconsistent form state
findings.body: shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators is forced to false for conditional UI, so IS_USER_IDENTIFIED is always false and ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS is never set, but shouldDisplayAuthenticators inherited from WebAuthnAuthenticator still returns true when context.getUser() != null. The login template can then be told to display authenticators with no list / as unidentified during re-authentication.
